results.title: In a NASA proposed nominal atmosphere of 34% oxygen and 0.56 atm, a BRE flame appeared to be steady after about 100 s.
results.claim: In a NASA proposed nominal atmosphere of 34% oxygen and 0.56 atm, a BRE flame appeared to be steady after about 100 s.
results.quote: Figure 9. Flame growth from ignition to steady state in test 19070D1. The conditions are ethylene/N2, hc = 24 kJ/g, 4.95 g/m2s, 34% O2, 8.2 psia, L = 2.42 kJ/g, steady. Figure 9 shows steady results for a NASA proposed nominal atmosphere of 34% oxygen and 0.56 atm. After about 100 s the flame appears to be steady.

results.title: For the ISS flames in its reported extinction analysis, Flame Design gives a critical extinction temperature of 1130 K, with fuel mass flux of 0.2 g/m2-s for normal flames and oxygen mass flux of 0.68 g/m2-s for inverse flames.
results.claim: For the ISS flames in its reported extinction analysis, Flame Design gives a critical extinction temperature of 1130 K, with fuel mass flux of 0.2 g/m2-s for normal flames and oxygen mass flux of 0.68 g/m2-s for inverse flames.
results.quote: All the ISS flames observed by this project extinguish at a critical extinction temperature of 1130 K, and at a fuel mass flux of 0.2 g/m2-s for normal flames, and at an oxygen mass flux of 0.68 g/m2-s for inverse flames.

results.title: Radiative extinction is observed when, at constant reactant flow rate, the flame expands until radiation heat loss approaches the chemical heat release.
results.claim: Radiative extinction is observed when, at constant reactant flow rate, the flame expands until radiation heat loss approaches the chemical heat release.
results.quote: Radiative extinction is observed when, at constant reactant flow rate, a flame expands until radiation heat loss approaches the chemical heat release.

results.title: Large BRE flames extinguished because of radiative heat loss, while small flames quenched at a second limit.
results.claim: Large BRE flames extinguished because of radiative heat loss, while small flames quenched at a second limit.
results.quote: Large flames extinguished due to radiative heat loss, while small flames quenched at a second limit.

results.title: Thin filament pyrometry of four BRE flames gave a critical temperature range for extinction of 1100 to 1200 K.
results.claim: Thin filament pyrometry of four BRE flames gave a critical temperature range for extinction of 1100 to 1200 K.
results.quote: TFP measurements of four flames confirmed that critical temperature range for extinction is 1100 to 1200 K. This is confirmed by numerical simulations.

results.title: Dilution limits for both methane and ethylene coflow flames were extended in microgravity: the flames are more stable and stay lifted at lower fuel concentrations.
results.claim: Dilution limits for both methane and ethylene coflow flames were extended in microgravity: the flames are more stable and stay lifted at lower fuel concentrations.
results.quote: Meanwhile, dilution limits for both methane and ethylene flames were extended in microgravity, where the microgravity flames are more stable, allowing for lifted flames at lower fuel concentrations.

results.title: Under some conditions the electric field was able to blow out flames.
results.claim: Under some conditions the electric field was able to blow out flames.
results.quote: The electric field was also able to blow out flames under some conditions.

results.title: Nitrogen-diluted methane and ethylene spherical flames in air seem to show kinetic extinction at low flow rates and radiative extinction at high flow rates.
results.claim: Nitrogen-diluted methane and ethylene spherical flames in air seem to show kinetic extinction at low flow rates and radiative extinction at high flow rates.
results.quote: Nitrogen-diluted methane and ethylene flames in air seem to demonstrate kinetic extinction at low flow rates (low system Da) and radiative extinction at high flow rates (high system Da). Such phenomena were not observed in our ground-based research, given the limited microgravity durations. Nevertheless, comparisons with computational simulations are needed to assess better the extinction behavior.

results.title: For mixtures with 20-30% ethylene, spherical non-sooty flames established at 3 cc/s underwent kinetic extinction on ramp down before reaching 1 cc/s and radiative extinction on ramp up before reaching 8 cc/s.
results.claim: For mixtures with 20-30% ethylene, spherical non-sooty flames established at 3 cc/s underwent kinetic extinction on ramp down before reaching 1 cc/s and radiative extinction on ramp up before reaching 8 cc/s.
results.quote: For mixtures with 20-30% C2H4 content, spherical non-sooty flames are established at 3 cc/s; and kinetic extinctions are observed during ramp down before reaching 1 cc/s. For the same mixtures, radiative extinctions are observed when the non-sooty flames are established at 3 cc/s and the flow rates are ramped up before reaching 8 cc/s.

results.title: Radiative extinction was found to be a common event in s-Flame ISS testing; it had been predicted computationally but not observed before for these flame conditions.
results.claim: Radiative extinction was found to be a common event in s-Flame ISS testing; it had been predicted computationally but not observed before for these flame conditions.
results.quote: Surprisingly, radiative extinction has been found to be a common event in ISS testing, which was predicted computationally, but not observed previously for our flame conditions.

results.title: Helium-diluted cases had shifted extinction limits compared with nitrogen-diluted cases, and ignition was severely affected by using helium as the diluent.
results.claim: Helium-diluted cases had shifted extinction limits compared with nitrogen-diluted cases, and ignition was severely affected by using helium as the diluent.
results.quote: Helium-diluted cases had shifted extinction limits with respect to the nitrogen-diluted cases. In general, kinetic extinction was difficult to observe for the conditions examined. Ignition was also severely affected by using He as diluent. More analyses are needed to assess instability near the flame limits, which was predicted to occur computationally.

results.title: Hot PMMA can keep supplying fuel after flame extinction.
results.claim: Hot PMMA can keep supplying fuel after flame extinction.
results.quote: After extinction, the hot material can continue to produce fuel for some time until it cools.

results.title: For thin PMMA films the opposed-flow extinction velocities were about 1 cm/s for 100, 200 and 300 micrometer thickness and about 1.5 cm/s for 400 micrometers.
results.claim: For thin PMMA films the opposed-flow extinction velocities were about 1 cm/s for 100, 200 and 300 micrometer thickness and about 1.5 cm/s for 400 micrometers.
results.quote: When tests are repeated with samples of different thicknesses, the extinction velocities are found to be about 1 cm/s for 100, 200, and 300 μm and about 1.5 cm/s for 400 μm.

results.title: At about 16 percent O2 the extinction velocities were about 2.6 cm/s (100 micrometer film) and about 4 cm/s (200 micrometer film); the report concludes the extinction velocity increases significantly as O2 is reduced and is independent of fuel thickness.
results.claim: At about 16 percent O2 the extinction velocities were about 2.6 cm/s (100 micrometer film) and about 4 cm/s (200 micrometer film); the report concludes the extinction velocity increases significantly as O2 is reduced and is independent of fuel thickness.
results.quote: Tests were also conducted at a lower O2 level of about 16 percent for two different thicknesses and the extinction velocities were found to be about 2.6 cm/s for 100 μm and about 4 cm/s for 200 μm. It should be mentioned that the width of the sample was different, 20 mm for the 100-μm sample and 10 mm for the 200-μm sample. Even though there is insufficient data at the lower O2 level, it is clear that the extinction velocity significantly increases as the O2 level is reduced and is independent of the fuel thickness.

results.title: Sustained flame spread was not observed for opposed-flow velocities below approximately 4 mm/s for the 6.35 mm and 9.525 mm diameter black PMMA rods.
results.claim: Sustained flame spread was not observed for opposed-flow velocities below approximately 4 mm/s for the 6.35 mm and 9.525 mm diameter black PMMA rods.
results.quote: Sustained flame spread for the conditions tested was not observed for opposed-flow velocities below approximately 4 mm/s for the 0.00635- and 0.009525-m- diameter rods.

results.title: After extinction the hot PMMA can keep producing fuel for some time until it cools, and premixed flame oscillations along the rod persist much longer in microgravity than in normal gravity; the report says suppression efforts should be maintained until the burning material has cooled and stopped emitting vapors.
results.claim: After extinction the hot PMMA can keep producing fuel for some time until it cools, and premixed flame oscillations along the rod persist much longer in microgravity than in normal gravity; the report says suppression efforts should be maintained until the burning material has cooled and stopped emitting vapors.
results.quote: After extinction, the hot material can continue to produce fuel for some time until it cools. Premixed flame oscillations along the rod have been observed for the concurrent rod geometry that persist much longer in microgravity than in normal gravity due to the lower rate of convective cooling of the rod. This suggests that spacecraft fire suppression efforts should be maintained until the burning material has cooled and stopped emitting vapors.

results.title: The RTDFS tests run in BASS-II vindicated the theoretical and computational finding that the critical opposed-flow velocity for radiative extinction in microgravity is independent of fuel thickness.
results.claim: The RTDFS tests run in BASS-II vindicated the theoretical and computational finding that the critical opposed-flow velocity for radiative extinction in microgravity is independent of fuel thickness.
results.quote: RTDFS vindicated the theoretical and computational findings that the critical opposed-flow velocity at which radiative extinction occurs in a microgravity environment is independent of fuel thickness

results.title: For n-dodecane droplets in CFI, increased helium dilution led to earlier cool flame extinction, giving a larger extinction diameter.
results.claim: For n-dodecane droplets in CFI, increased helium dilution led to earlier cool flame extinction, giving a larger extinction diameter.
results.quote: Figure 5 illustrates the effect of helium dilution on the extinction diameter for n-dodecane. Increase helium dilution leads to earlier cool flame extinction giving a larger extinction diameter.

results.title: ISS droplet experiments in which some of the ambient nitrogen was replaced by carbon dioxide, helium or xenon show that different diluents act very differently on cool-flame combustion: the cool-flame extinction diameter is drastically increased with helium dilution compared to N2, CO2 or Xe, and that Xe dilution leads to longer burning with a smaller extinction diameter.
results.claim: ISS droplet experiments in which some of the ambient nitrogen was replaced by carbon dioxide, helium or xenon show that different diluents act very differently on cool-flame combustion: the cool-flame extinction diameter is drastically increased with helium dilution compared to N2, CO2 or Xe, and that Xe dilution leads to longer burning with a smaller extinction diameter.
results.quote: In these ISS experiments, some of the nitrogen in the ambient gas mixture is replaced by an inert gas, namely, carbon dioxide, helium, or xenon. Different diluents were observed to exert remarkably different influences on the cool-flame combustion of fuel droplets. The results show that the cool-flame extinction diameter is drastically increased with helium dilution compared to N2, CO2 or Xe, and Xe dilution leads to longer burning with a smaller extinction diameter.

results.title: The same study concludes that xenon decreases burning rates substantially but can sustain cool flames at much lower oxygen concentrations compared to helium.
results.claim: The same study concludes that xenon decreases burning rates substantially but can sustain cool flames at much lower oxygen concentrations compared to helium.
results.quote: Xenon decreases burning rates substantially, but can sustain cool flames at much lower oxygen concentrations compared to helium.

results.title: ISS droplet tests found that diluent choice changes cool-flame behavior.
results.claim: ISS droplet tests found that diluent choice changes cool-flame behavior.
results.quote: Different diluents were observed to exert remarkably different influences on the cool-flame combustion of fuel droplets.

results.title: The preliminary SLICE findings say microgravity flames were generally wider and less likely to lift off than their 1g counterparts, and more highly diluted flames could be stabilized in microgravity.
results.claim: The preliminary SLICE findings say microgravity flames were generally wider and less likely to lift off than their 1g counterparts, and more highly diluted flames could be stabilized in microgravity.
results.quote: Due to the lack of buoyancy force, the microgravity (0g) flames are generally wider and less likely to lift off than their 1 g counterparts, and flames with higher dilution levels can be stabilized in microgravity.

results.title: For a pair of diluted flames shown in the SLICE report, the 1g flame was lifted while its 0g counterpart was attached and even formed a small soot cone.
results.claim: For a pair of diluted flames shown in the SLICE report, the 1g flame was lifted while its 0g counterpart was attached and even formed a small soot cone.
results.quote: For the diluted flames, the 1g flame is lifted while its 0g counterpart is attached, and a small soot cone is even formed in the 0g flame.

results.title: A status note in the SLICE final report says the microgravity flames lifted at significantly greater velocities than the normal-gravity flames but were much less stable once lifted.
results.claim: A status note in the SLICE final report says the microgravity flames lifted at significantly greater velocities than the normal-gravity flames but were much less stable once lifted.
results.quote: The microgravity flames have lifted at significantly greater velocities than the normal-gravity flames, but upon lifting have been much less stable.

results.title: In SLICE, as the flow was slowly increased toward the lift-off limit the flame detached from the burner, in some cases stabilizing above it but often blowing out.
results.claim: In SLICE, as the flow was slowly increased toward the lift-off limit the flame detached from the burner, in some cases stabilizing above it but often blowing out.
results.quote: Generally, the flow was slowly increased as the flame approached the liftoff limit where it detaches from the burner and in some cases stabilizes above the burner but often blows out (i.e., extinguishes) as in this example.
